Over the concluding stages had difficulty obtaining clear running when being shifted to the inside of LAHORE.  When questioned regarding his riding from near the 300 Metres Z Purton stated that after being crossed by LAHORE in the early stages he elected to shift to that runner’s outside where he was positioned between LAHORE and the favourite TURQUOISE VELOCITY.  He said near the 300 Metres he elected to shift in slightly to follow TURQUOISE VELOCITY as he felt that runner would provide him with the opportunity to improve into the event.  He said when TURQUOISE VELOCITY shifted in slightly leaving the 300 Metres and did not respond to its rider’s efforts to improve, he then was required to steady and shift back to the outside of TURQUOISE VELOCITY to obtain clear running.  After considering his explanation the Stewards found the tactics adopted by Jockey Purton were reasonable in the circumstances.
No report.

Shortly after the start was bumped by LUCKY SECRET.  Near the 300  Metres SIGHT HERMOSO improved to the outside of LIVE WIRE when that runner shifted in whilst following TURQUOISE VELOCITY.  When TURQUOISE VELOCITY then commenced to give ground, LIVE WIRE (Z Purton) shifted out, resulting in SIGHT HERMOSO being taken out onto SUPREME VOYAGER which was steadied.  Z Purton was advised to exercise more care.  Noted to have lost its right front plate after the race.
No report.

On jumping made heavy contact with LUCKY SECRET and became unbalanced.  M L Yeung stated that his mount became stirred up behind the starting gates due to the delay when TOP MAESTRO was withdrawn.  He said his mount travelled only fairly during the race and under its top weight of 135 lbs found it difficult to finish the race off when under pressure in the Home Straight.  Trainer K W Lui stated that the horse had pleased him leading into the race and concurred with the views of Jockey Yeung that the pre-race manners of the horse had affected its performance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of TURQUOISE VELOCITY, a last start winner, was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, TURQUOISE VELOCITY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

When questioned regarding his riding H Bowman stated that the intention was to hold a handy position behind the leaders from a favourable barrier and with the horse stepping up to 1400 Metres.  He said FLOW WATER FLOW jumped reasonably well but in the early stages was positioned to the inside of DASHING MAURISON which was being ridden hard to hold a more forward position.  He said when the pace of the event was being run inside of standard time he would have had to make use of his mount in the early stages to hold a more forward position and as he was concerned this would result in FLOW WATER FLOW racing keenly, particularly having regard to its inexperience and having its first race start at Sha Tin, he elected to allow DASHING MAURISON to cross his mount near the 1100 Metres.  He said whilst he had not expected this would result in his mount settling at the rear of the field he felt this was the best option for the horse to allow it to race where comfortable and have a good opportunity to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  He added throughout the middle stages FLOW WATER FLOW travelled well and after shifting to the outside upon entering the Home Straight the horse ran on well under riding.  Trainer J Size stated that whilst he had expected FLOW WATER FLOW to hold a more forward position, given the horse is lightly raced and does not have an established racing pattern he was comfortable with Jockey Bowman’s decision to allow the horse to settle towards the rear of the field.  After considering his explanation and taking into account the sectional times of the event and the relative inexperience of the horse, the Stewards found the tactics adopted by Jockey Bowman were reasonable in the circumstances.  Sent for sampling post-race.

He said as a consequence SERAPH GABRIEL took some time to rebalance before finishing the race off reasonably well over the final 200 Metres.
